You are checking an operations research model before it is solved. Read the word problem and list what any correct formulation of it must contain. Don't write the model, and don't solve the problem.

The model's decision variables are listed by name in <variables>. Use exactly those names and no others. If a requirement needs a quantity that isn't one of them, put it in cannot_express instead.

- variables: for each listed name, say whether it counts whole things ("integer": vehicles, trips, people, products, servings), measures a divisible quantity ("continuous": kilograms, acres, hours, money), or the text supports both ("unclear"). Quote the words that decide it.
- objective: its direction (min or max) and its terms over the listed names, with the numbers exactly as given. Quote the words it comes from.
- requirements: every requirement the text states, as a linear inequality or equation over the listed names. Use the numbers exactly as given, and write percentages as fractions (30% as 0.3). Quote the exact words each one comes from.
  - strict: true if the wording is strict ("more than", "must exceed", "fewer than"); still write it with >= or <=.
  - could_be_equal: true if the wording names no inequality at all ("twice as many as", "three times the number of"), so "=" would be a fair reading too.
  - scope: "combined" if one limit covers several items together, "per item" if it applies to each item separately, "single" if it involves one quantity. Decide this from the text: "at most 50 cakes of either type" may be one total or one limit per type, so quote why.
  - Leave out non-negativity, unless the text says a quantity can be negative.
- not_requirements: every sentence that states a preference, a motivation, popularity, or background rather than a requirement ("prefers", "is more popular", "would like", "sells better"), with its quote, why it isn't a requirement, and the inequality someone might wrongly make of it (empty terms if there's none). Never turn one of these into a requirement.
- cannot_express: each requirement that needs a quantity not among the listed names, with its quote and the quantity it needs.
- Don't add anything the text doesn't state.

<problem>
For manufacturing companies, it is important to develop appropriate production plans and human resource management strategies to reduce operating costs, inventory costs, stockout costs, and labor costs. In particular, for products with high demand fluctuations, companies need to accurately forecast demand and develop corresponding production plans. A company produces a folding table, with a raw material cost of 90 yuan per unit and 5 labor hours. The unit price of the product is 300 yuan. At the beginning of January, the company has 1000 workers and holds 15,000 units of inventory. The normal wage for workers is 30 yuan per hour, and the normal working hours per worker per day is 8 hours. Overtime hours are paid at an hourly rate of 40 yuan. The number of working days per month is calculated as 20 days. Assuming the company has sufficient available production machines and its production capacity is not limited by machine hours. The overtime hours per worker per month do not exceed 20 hours. Holding inventory incurs corresponding inventory costs. If there is a stockout due to insufficient capacity, there will be certain stockout costs. In addition, the company can make up for the shortage through outsourcing. The outsourcing cost per unit, monthly inventory cost, and monthly stockout cost are 200 yuan, 15 yuan, and 35 yuan, respectively. The company's employees are all temporary workers, and the company can flexibly decide the number of employees to hire and dismiss each month. The cost of hiring and dismissing a single employee is 5000 yuan and 8000 yuan, respectively. Assuming the company has used existing forecasting models to predict the demand from month 1 to month 6, as shown in Table 4.1.

Table 4.1: Demand Forecast

| Month | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Demand Forecast | 20000 | 40000 | 42000 | 35000 | 19000 | 18500 |

Please develop a production plan, worker schedule, and plan for hiring and dismissing employees for the company to maximize its total net profit over 6 months, while ensuring that the company holds at least 10,000 units of product by the end of June.
</problem>
